findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-ground the no-shadowing invariant on load_eval_spec's real precedence: since .rebar/evals/<id>.eval.yaml WINS over packaged specs (eval.py:74-78), check that no written prompt-id collides with a PACKAGED built-in (compare against `ls src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/` prompt-ids and existing .rebar/evals/ ids), and define 'criterion with no existing spec' as resolving in NEITHER directory.
evidence: eval.py:76-78 — `path = eval_spec_path(prompt_id, repo_root); if not path.is_file(): path = _packaged_eval_spec(prompt_id)` — the .rebar/evals path is tried first and wins when present

eval.py:57-60 — eval_spec_path returns `.rebar/evals/<id>.eval.yaml`; docstring: 'A user .rebar/evals/<id>.eval.yaml (git-tracked beside the prompt) WINS; otherwise a packaged built-in spec is used' (load_eval_spec docstring lines 74-75)
Plan writes to '.rebar/evals/<prompt-id>.eval.yaml' (Disposition section) — the same user dir that overrides packaged specs
`.rebar/evals/` already contains plan-review-project-*.eval.yaml files, confirming it is the live precedence-winning user-spec directory, not an empty scratch dir
The AC intersects only against packaged dir src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/, which a .rebar/evals/ write never intersects even when it shadows a same-id packaged built-in
findings.finding: The no-shadowing invariant (Scope + AC line 5) checks the wrong directory and rests on a false premise about load_eval_spec resolution order. load_eval_spec (eval.py:71-78) resolves the USER spec at .rebar/evals/<id>.eval.yaml FIRST — via eval_spec_path (eval.py:57-60) — and that user spec WINS over the packaged built-in; the packaged dir src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/ is only the fallback. The plan writes mined specs into .rebar/evals/, so a mined prompt-id that collides with a PACKAGED built-in would silently shadow it, exactly the outcome the plan claims is impossible ('load_eval_spec never resolves a mined file in place of a packaged one'). The AC's intersection test against `ls src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/` cannot detect this, because a written .rebar/evals/ file never shares that packaged directory yet still overrides its contents at load time.
findings.location: Scope section ('load_eval_spec (eval.py:69-78) never resolves a mined file in place of a packaged one') and Acceptance Criteria line 5 ('shares no member with ls src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/')
scenarios: A mined criterion's prompt-id matches a packaged built-in spec name; the written .rebar/evals/ file overrides the shipped spec on every subsequent load_eval_spec call, and the AC's src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/ intersection reports empty (a false all-clear).
findings.suggested_fix: State the invariant as: a mined prompt-id must not equal any packaged built-in spec id NOR any existing .rebar/evals/ id; verify by asserting the written prompt-id set is disjoint from the union of both directories' ids (not just the packaged src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/ path), because the write target .rebar/evals/ is precisely the directory that overrides packaged specs at load time.

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile the failure model: name the concrete fatal condition (other than pre-flight BudgetExceeded) that leaves completed criteria requiring reconcile-on-resume, or drop the 'resume at first uncompleted criterion' guarantee that pre-flight refusal cannot produce.
evidence: Plan: 'The run pre-flights through ledger.reserve(estimate_usd, ...)' (singular, whole-run)
Plan: 'BudgetExceeded from the pre-flight is FATAL and non-retryable'
Plan: 'On a fatal error the run stops with completed criteria admitted and their spend reconciled ... so a re-run resumes at the first uncompleted criterion'
ledger.reserve raises before any finalize/model call (ledger.py:86-111); a pre-flight refusal produces no completed criteria
findings.finding: The failure-disposition model is internally inconsistent: the only named FATAL error is BudgetExceeded from the single pre-flight reserve(), which by design runs BEFORE any criterion executes (AC-3 asserts zero model calls), so a fatal stop can never leave 'completed criteria admitted' to reconcile or a 'first uncompleted criterion' to resume from.
scenarios: Ledger already near ceiling: reserve() raises, nothing has run — resume/reconcile path described in AC-7 has no partial state to act on
A mid-run transport failure (the RETRYABLE case) is the only thing that could leave partial completion, but the plan classes it as retried-within-run, not a stop
findings.suggested_fix: State that reserve() is called PER CRITERION (or per batch) so a mid-run BudgetExceeded can leave earlier criteria completed and finalized; then AC-7's resume-via-reconcile has a real trigger.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the `DET` estimate-key branch with the runner's `pass1_chunk` execution path: either state that plan-review criteria are never `exec:DET` (drop the DET case) or define how a DET criterion is actually executed and finalized given ADR 0033's stripping/code-scan behavior.
evidence: Plan: "The per-criterion estimate key is chosen from its `exec` tier in `criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')` … `DET` map[s] to `criteria-eval-cheap`. A `DET` criterion's finder is deterministic and issues no priced model call, so it is finalized at its real (zero-cost) usage."

ADR 0033: "DET criteria are stripped before the prose pass. `orchestrator.route_criteria` … removes `exec:DET` criteria before `pass1_chunk` — the prose finder never sees them" and "The DET engine scans code, not plan prose."

Runner path drives every candidate through the prose finder: `passes.pass1_chunk(runner, cfg, plan=plan, chunk=[desc], …)` (src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:139-142); plan states "execute the criterion's real Pass-1 finder … one `passes.pass1_chunk` call per case per run."

Plan-review `criteria_routing.json` exec values are only `1-TURN`/`2-STEP`/`AGENT` (no `DET`); `registry.exec_tier` docstring: "`DET` is owned by det_floor; here we return one of `AGENT` / `2-STEP` / `1-TURN`" (registry.py:604-610).
ADR 0016 permits project-supplied `exec:DET` criteria, so a DET criterion can be an in-scope "criterion with no existing spec."
findings.finding: The Budget-enforcement decision rule maps a plan-review `exec: DET` criterion to `criteria-eval-cheap` and specifies a deterministic zero-cost finalize, but this is unreachable/incorrect for the runner's own execution path: the runner drives every candidate through `passes.pass1_chunk` (eval_solver.py:139), while ADR 0033 records as verified architecture that `exec:DET` criteria are stripped before `pass1_chunk` and that the DET engine scans code, not plan prose. The packaged plan-review `criteria_routing.json` also has no `exec: DET` entry (only 1-TURN/2-STEP/AGENT), and `registry.exec_tier` documents that it never returns DET. A project-overlay DET criterion with no existing spec would fall in scope yet could not take the described zero-cost path.
findings.location: Approach → Budget enforcement ("`1-TURN`, `2-STEP` and `DET` map to `criteria-eval-cheap` … A `DET` criterion's finder is deterministic and issues no priced model call, so it is finalized at its real (zero-cost) usage.")
scenarios: A project overlay registers an `exec:DET` plan-review criterion that has no packaged eval spec; the admission runner treats it as in scope, selects `criteria-eval-cheap`, and drives it through `pass1_chunk` — which never runs a DET finder — so it neither fires nor 'finalizes at zero-cost' as the plan claims.
findings.suggested_fix: Since plan-review `exec:DET` criteria are stripped before `pass1_chunk` (ADR 0033) and the packaged routing has none, remove the `DET` branch from the estimate-key rule and state that in-scope criteria are LLM finders (1-TURN/2-STEP/AGENT); if project DET criteria must be admissible, specify a distinct deterministic execution path (not `pass1_chunk`) and how their zero-cost usage is finalized.

findings.checklist_item: Add an acceptance criterion proving that a criterion whose reproducing candidates are one-sided is withheld to the drift report and writes no .eval.yaml.
evidence: The disposition rule states a criterion is withheld when its surviving dataset is unbalanced
No AC in the Acceptance Criteria list covers the unbalanced-dataset withholding outcome — the reproduce/withhold ACs are per-candidate, not per-criterion-balance
findings.finding: The plan describes a distinct disposition outcome — a criterion whose reproducing candidates do NOT form a balanced (both-sides-non-empty) dataset is withheld entirely to the drift report rather than written as a spec — but no acceptance criterion exercises or proves this path.
findings.location: Disposition paragraph: 'a criterion's spec is written ... only when its reproducing candidates still form a balanced (both-sides-non-empty) dataset; otherwise the whole criterion is withheld to the drift report'
scenarios: A criterion where all must-not-fire candidates fail to reproduce, leaving a fire-only dataset — silently written as an invalid one-sided spec if the balance check is never proven
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'Against a criterion whose surviving candidates are all must-fire (or all must-not-fire), the criterion is withheld and a drift-report entry recorded; verified by pytest asserting no spec file exists and the report names the criterion.'

findings.checklist_item: Specify the per-criterion run_id derivation (e.g. deterministic from run identity + criterion prompt_id) so reconcile matches the same key on re-run and AC-7's 'zero new calls' holds.
evidence: Plan: 'reconciled into the ledger (via reconcile, keyed by run_id), so a re-run resumes at the first uncompleted criterion'
reconcile: 'for existing in _read_ledger(...): if existing.get("run_id") == run_id: return existing' (ledger.py:195-197)
finalize/reconcile take a single run_id + candidate; the plan finalizes 'priced usage per criterion' but does not define the per-criterion run_id
findings.finding: Resume-without-recharge via reconcile requires each completed criterion to carry a STABLE, deterministic run_id that a re-run reproduces, but the plan never specifies how run_id is derived per criterion; reconcile only returns an existing row when run_id matches exactly (ledger.py:195-197).
scenarios: Re-run after a stop: if run_id is per-run (not per-criterion) or non-deterministic, reconcile will not match the prior criterion's row and will re-charge it

evidence: Plan cites "`eval_solver.py:139-142`" and "`load_eval_spec` (`eval.py:69-78`)"
list_directory src/rebar/llm/ shows no eval_solver.py / eval.py at top level; both exist under src/rebar/llm/evals/ (line numbers 139-142 and 69-78 do match the real files there)
findings.finding: The plan cites the two load-bearing modules by bare filename (`eval_solver.py:139-142`, `eval.py:69-78`) as though they sit at `src/rebar/llm/`, but both files live at `src/rebar/llm/evals/`; the top-level directory contains no `eval_solver.py` or `eval.py`.
scenarios: A reader resolves the cited path at src/rebar/llm/ and finds nothing, wasting time locating the real module.

findings.checklist_item: State the retry bound (max attempts and whether spend counts against the cap) for transient errors in the Failure disposition section.
evidence: Retry is asserted with no cap on attempts
A missing bound is a defaultable gap under E2 signal (5) unstated constraints
findings.finding: The failure-disposition rule declares transient model/transport errors RETRYABLE and 'retried within the run' but states no retry bound (max attempts / backoff), leaving the executor to invent one.
findings.location: Failure disposition: 'A transient model or transport error is RETRYABLE and retried within the run.'
scenarios: A persistently flaky transport could retry unboundedly, silently consuming budget against the $250 ceiling
findings.suggested_fix: State a default, e.g. 'retried up to N times with backoff; exhausted retries are treated as a non-reproducing run for that epoch,' and note retried calls still count toward the ledger cap.

evidence: Subject: 'For each mined candidate case, execute the criterion's real Pass-1 finder ... A reproducing candidate is kept in its criterion's dataset'

Prerequisite: 'An emitter that reads the manifest and writes one `.eval.yaml` per criterion into a working directory for the sibling admission runner' with a full dataset, gold_set, epochs:3, gate:at_least(2)
Subject builds the balanced dataset by admitting/withholding candidates, but the prerequisite emitter already enforces balance and emits the complete spec before admission
findings.finding: The subject plan describes reading in-memory 'mined candidate cases' with predicted behavior and driving the solver over them, then keeping reproducing candidates 'in its criterion's dataset' and writing the spec. But the prerequisite emitter already writes complete, strict-valid `.eval.yaml` specs (with dataset, gold_set, epochs, gate, scorers) to a working directory. The subject's model of admission — running loose 'candidate cases' and assembling a dataset from those that reproduce — is inconsistent with the prerequisite's output, which is a fully-formed per-criterion spec file, not a bag of individual candidate cases carrying per-case predictions.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the `run_case` invocation to pass `runner=` and `repo_root=` as keyword arguments (they are keyword-only in `eval_solver.run_case`).
evidence: Plan: "execute the criterion's real Pass-1 finder directly through its solver — `eval_solver.run_case(prompt_id, case, runner, repo_root)`"
src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:322-324: `def run_case(prompt_id: str, case: dict, *, runner: Runner, graph: bool = False, repo_root: str | None = None)` — `*` makes runner/repo_root keyword-only
findings.finding: The plan invokes `eval_solver.run_case(prompt_id, case, runner, repo_root)` with `runner` and `repo_root` as positional arguments, but the real signature is `run_case(prompt_id, case, *, runner, graph=False, repo_root=None)` — both `runner` and `repo_root` are keyword-only, so the call as written raises TypeError.
scenarios: Author codes the admission runner literally against the plan's positional call and hits a TypeError on first invocation.
findings.suggested_fix: Write the call as `eval_solver.run_case(prompt_id, case, runner=runner, repo_root=repo_root)`.

findings.checklist_item: State the effective ceiling explicitly (pass reserve_usd=0 to make 250 the true ceiling, or document that the default 30 reserve yields a ~220 spendable limit) so the budget claim and AC-3 boundary are exact.
evidence: Plan: 'ledger.reserve(estimate_usd, ledger_path=<epic ledger>, cap_usd=250.0)' (no reserve_usd)
reserve: 'remaining = cap - reserve_headroom - spent' with reserve_headroom defaulting to LEDGER_RESERVE_USD (ledger.py:103-105)
LEDGER_RESERVE_USD = 30.0 (ledger.py:30)
findings.finding: The plan calls reserve() with cap_usd=250.0 but omits reserve_usd, so the default LEDGER_RESERVE_USD=30 applies, making the effective spendable ceiling 220, not 250 — the 'Hard cap $250' and AC-8 'at most 250.0' understate the point at which reserve() will refuse.
findings.location: Approach → Budget enforcement; Budget section; AC-3
scenarios: Spend approaches ~220: reserve() raises BudgetExceeded even though the stated $250 cap is not reached, surprising the operator
findings.suggested_fix: Pass reserve_usd=0.0 alongside cap_usd=250.0 if $250 is meant to be the true hard ceiling.
